slots_and_copies.name: slot_0_header_block
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: unknown - no reader code traced; this is the only densely-populated region (EEPROM lines 0-3) in the 512-byte device

slots_and_copies.name: line_28_isolated_marker
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: unknown - single 8-byte line at offset 0xE0 byte-for-byte identical to the sentinel pattern at 0x18; could be a second slot/record header or an unrelated marker

checksums.name: unresolved_candidate_scan
checksums.formula_detail: Brute-force sum8/xor8 scan over all byte positions in the populated region (offsets 0x00-0x1F and 0xE0-0xE7) against all contiguous sub-ranges produced 1888 coincidental matches on the single available .sav sample. With n=1 sample the search space is underdetermined; no specific formula/offset pairing could be distinguished from coincidence. No checksum/CRC function exists in the traced decompiled code (ghidra/decompiled.c, ghidra/save_related_functions.c report 0 save-I/O seeds).

fields.name: identity_tag_reversed
fields.evidence: Raw bytes 33 31 30 30 45 41 33 42 byte-reverse to ASCII 'B3AE0013', which is this release's game code (B3AE) plus literal digits '0013'. Interpretation as a deliberate identity/version stamp vs. a byte-order artifact of the capture tool's EEPROM-line serialization cannot be adjudicated without decompiled writer code or a second sample.

fields.name: candidate_counter_or_flags_u32
fields.evidence: Only non-zero, non-magic 32-bit value in the populated block; no corroborating code or second sample to confirm role.

fields.name: candidate_u16_field_a
fields.evidence: Isolated small integer value adjacent to the counter candidate at offset 0x08; no structure proof available.

fields.name: candidate_packed_flag_u16_a
fields.evidence: High bit (0x8000) set, consistent with a common GBA packed valid/enabled-flag-plus-value convention, but unconfirmed by code.

fields.name: candidate_packed_flag_u16_b
fields.evidence: High bit (0x8000) set, same pattern as offset 0x0E; relationship between the two u16 values not resolved (byte-swap/arithmetic checks did not cleanly match).

fields.name: zero_padding_block
fields.evidence: All-zero region with no visible structure; could be reserved/padding.

fields.name: sentinel_pattern_primary
fields.evidence: Identical to the pattern at offset 0xE0 (line 28); candidate terminator/sentinel or secondary-record header.

fields.name: erased_region_main
fields.evidence: Direct byte-level observation of the .sav file; standard EEPROM erased-cell fill value.

fields.name: sentinel_pattern_isolated
fields.evidence: Byte-for-byte identical to sentinel_pattern_primary (offset 0x18); isolated inside an otherwise fully-erased span, suggesting deliberate placement rather than noise.

fields.name: erased_region_tail
fields.evidence: Direct byte-level observation of the .sav file; standard EEPROM erased-cell fill value.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip one byte of the reversed 'B3AE0013' identity tag (e.g. byte at 0x00 from 0x33 to 0xAA)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: if a genuine identity/version check, game should reject/reset the save; if a dump-tooling artifact only, no gameplay effect

fuzzing_targets.mutation: increment u32_le candidate counter from 0x00000400 to 0x00000401
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: no visible change if a free-running counter; save rejection or auto-repair if actually a checksum

fuzzing_targets.mutation: clear high bit of both candidate packed-flag u16 values (0x8099->0x0099, 0x9889->0x1889)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: if high bit is a valid/enabled flag, associated feature/slot should appear disabled or reset after reload
if a terminator, reader may begin treating subsequent blank lines as valid data or exhibit boundary errors

fuzzing_targets.mutation: zero out isolated sentinel pattern at 0xE0
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: if an independent second-slot header, that slot should appear empty/unused; if unrelated padding, no effect

fuzzing_targets.mutation: write non-0xFF filler (0x00 x8) into a currently-blank line (first line of the erased main region)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: reveals whether the reader scans the full 512 bytes or only fixed line ranges, clarifying actual slot/record geometry

open_questions: Is the media truly eeprom512, or could the 512-byte capture reflect only a partial/initial write of a larger SRAM/Flash device? (No driver code traced to confirm access method.)
Is the byte-reversed 'B3AE0013' string a deliberate game-written identity/version stamp, or an artifact of how the capture tool serialized the 8-byte EEPROM line?
What do the u32 field at 0x08 and the two u16 fields at 0x0E/0x10 actually represent (counter, flags, checksum, or gameplay data)?
Are the two identical 'FF 00x7' sentinel patterns at offsets 0x18 and 0xE0 functionally linked (e.g., slot headers), or coincidental?
What is the true slot/record geometry across the 64 EEPROM lines, given only 2 of 64 lines are populated in this single sample?

No checksum/CRC algorithm could be identified; resolving this requires either decompiled save-I/O code (trace must cover ROM address 0x08A0A404, the EEPROM_V124 tag site) or multiple independent .sav samples for cross-sample differencing.
Zero paired .ss save states exist for this release, so none of the fuzzing_targets mutations above have been (or currently can be) replayed/observed in a live emulator session.
